## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Prioritize this server when the user mentions Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or provides figma.com URLs.

Capabilities:
- Read designs FROM Figma (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Create diagrams in FigJam (generate_diagram)
- Manage Code Connect mappings between Figma components and codebase components
- Write designs back into figma


WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user shares a Figma URL (figma.com/design/..., figma.com/board/..., figma.com/make/...)
- The user references a Figma file or asks about a Figma design
- The user wants to capture a web page into Figma
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName → FigJam file, use get_figjam

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW:

Step 1 — Get the design:
Call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey. This is your primary tool.
It returns code, a screenshot, and contextual hints.

Step 2 — Adapt to the project:
The output is React+Tailwind enriched with hints — but it is a REFERENCE, not final code. Always adapt to the target project's stack, components, and conventions.
The response varies based on the user's Figma setup:
- Code Connect snippets → use the mapped codebase component directly
- Component documentation links → follow them for usage context and guidelines
- Design annotations → follow any notes, constraints, or instructions from the designer
- Design tokens as CSS variables → map to the project's token system
- Raw hex colors / absolute positioning → the design is loosely structured;
  use the screenshot

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

글로벌 Claude 문서(CLAUDE.md, RTK.md, settings.json) 리뷰입니다.

## 핵심 이슈

### 1. RTK 내용 중복 — CLAUDE.md 비대화 (우선순위 높음)
- [CLAUDE.md:67](C:/Users/nineonelabs003/.claude/CLAUDE.md#L67)에서 `@RTK.md` 임포트하는데, 바로 아래 [73-205줄](C:/Users/nineonelabs003/.claude/CLAUDE.md#L73-L205)에 `<!-- rtk-instructions v2 -->` 블록이 통째로 인라인되어 있습니다. `rtk init --global`이 자동 삽입한 것으로 보이는데, **같은 내용을 두 번 로드** 중입니다.
- 결과: CLAUDE.md가 205줄 — 본인이 AGENTS.md에 정한 "CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md ≤ 200 lines" 원칙보다 글로벌 단독으로 더 큼. 매 세션마다 토큰 낭비.
- 또한 두 RTK 문서가 **표현이 미묘하게 달라서** (RTK.md는 "MUST Prefix" 표 / 인라인은 워크플로우 분류) 차이날 때 어느 쪽이 정답인지 헷갈립니다.
- **권장**: 인라인 블록(73-205줄) 제거, `@RTK.md` 임포트만 남기기.

### 2. C 드라이브 표현이 misleading
- [CLAUDE.md:20](C:/Users/nineonelabs003/.claude/CLAUDE.md#L20) "All Claude data lives on **C drive** under the standard user profile location"
- 실제 의도는 "`%USERPROFILE%\.claude\` (C든 D든 사용자 프로필 위치)"이지만, 다른 머신·계정으로 이전 시 C 드라이브 가정이 깨집니다. AGENTS.md에서는 정확히 `%USERPROFILE%`라고 표현 — 글로벌도 동일하게 통일하는 게 안전.

### 3. FOMO 가드 vs 실제 훅 8개 — 자기모순 위험
- [CLAUDE.md:18](C:/Users/nineonelabs003/.claude/CLAUDE.md#L18) "DON'T add hooks ... without a documented recurring need" + Vanilla compliance 원칙
- [settings.json](c:/Users/nineonelabs003/.claude/settings.json)에는 SessionStart/End/PostToolUse/UserPromptSubmit/PreCompact/PostCompact/Stop + statusLine = **8개 커스텀 훅** 등록.
- 50-61줄에 각 훅의 목적이 한 줄씩 적혀 있긴 하지만, "왜 vanilla 대신 필요한지(과거 사건/측정 효과)" 근거는 없음 → `/audit-harness` 분기 점검 시 이 훅들이 살아남을 근거를 메모해두면 좋습니다. 그렇지 않으면 본인 룰을 본인이 어김.

### 4. 참조 문서 존재 검증 필요
- CLAUDE.md가 참조: `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `AUTOMATION.md`, `templates\order-match-checklist.md`, `templates\project-init.md`
- 메모리에는 이런 파일이 인덱스되어 있지 않습니다. 참조만 남고 파일이 없거나 stale하면 "찾으라"는 안내가 거짓말이 됩니다. 한 번 정합성 확인 권장.

### 5. settings.json 사소한 점
- `Read(**/.env*)` 와 `Read(**/credentials.json)`은 OK. 단, `Read(.credentials*)`는 **루트만** 매칭 — 하위 디렉토리 `.credentials`는 빠집니다. `Read(**/.credentials*)`로 통일 권장.
- `agentPushNotifEnabled: false`인데 본인이 `/loop`·`/schedule` 자주 쓰면 백그라운드 알림이 필요할 수 있음 — 의도면 무시.

### 6. MEMORY 정합성
- `feedback_rtk.md`에 "WSL Remote = auto-rewrite hook, native Windows = explicit prefix"가 둘 다 들어 있는데 이 머신은 native Windows 단일 환경. 다른 머신용 정보가 섞이면 향후 혼란. 단일 머신만 쓴다면 WSL 절은 제거 권장.

## 잘 된 점
- Order Match Verification 절차([24-36줄](C:/Users/nineonelabs003/.claude/CLAUDE.md#L24-L36))는 명확하고 실행 가능.
- `permissions.deny`의 destructive 커맨드 커버리지 충실.

Perfect! Now I have comprehensive data. Let me create a detailed audit report with findings:

## **AUDIT REPORT: Project-Level Claude/AGENTS Rules vs. Global Config**

**Date**: 2026-04-28  
**Auditor**: Claude Code (READ-ONLY exploration)  
**Scope**: `/d/최신프로젝트/나인원랩스/퍼블/260427/` vs. `C:\Users\nineonelabs003\.claude\`

---

### **EXECUTIVE SUMMARY**

The project-level Claude rules are **architecturally sound** and mostly **consistent** with global config, with **one architectural edge case** (plans storage) that requires clarification and **one missing skill** (audit-harness) that is referenced but not implemented.

**Critical Findings**: 2  
**Minor Contradictions**: 1  
**Verification**: PASSED (200-line cap met)

---

### **1. DRIVE POLICY EDGE CASE: Plans Storage Location**

**Status**: ⚠️ **AMBIGUOUS BOUNDARY**

**Global Rule** (ARCHITECTURE.md:20-22):
```
Drive layout | **C drive only** for all Claude artifacts (no D / E split)
```

**Project Rule** (AGENTS.md:16):
```
- **D: drive only for project work.** Reads, writes, command execution, path references in project code or docs — all must stay on D:. Never reference `C:\`, `c:\`, `/mnt/c/` for project content.
```

**The Edge Case**:

Global ARCHITECTURE.md (§2, line 52-53) specifies:
```
├── plans/                                 # active + archived plans
```

And later (line 53):
```
├── projects/                              # per-project session state + memory
```

**Question**: When Claude opens this project and compacts the conversation, is the plan file written to:
- **`C:\Users\nineonelabs003\.claude\plans\ai-cozy-perlis-*.md`** (global Claude infra) — ALLOWED per AGENTS.md line 17
- Or **`D:\最新프ロ젝트\나인원랩스\퍼블\260427\.claude\plans\`** (project-local) — NOT IN ARCHITECTURE

**Finding**: AGENTS.md line 17 correctly exempts `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\` (global infra), but the **project memory folder** is ambiguous. ARCHITECTURE.md does not document a `projects/<projectname>/plans/` folder, only `projects/<projectname>/memory/`.

**Evidence**:
- AGENTS.md line 19: "New configs, plans (project-scoped), and project memory writes target D:."
- ARCHITECTURE.md line 52: "`plans/`" listed under global `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\`, not per-project
- Global CLAUDE.md line 13: "All paths in scripts derive from `$env:USERPROFILE` or `$env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` fallback"

**Recommendation**: Clarify in AGENTS.md whether "plans (project-scoped)" means:
1. Session plans go to C (global), OR
2. Project-specific worktree/feature branch plans go to D (project-scoped)

---

### **2. RTK RULE DUPLICATION & DRIFT**

**Status**: ✅ **CONSISTENT (with strategic duplication)**

**Files involved**:
- Global `CLAUDE.md` (lines 11, 63-67): "RTK on This Machine" section
- Global `RTK.md` (lines 1-128): Full reference
- Project `AGENTS.md` (lines 76-96): "RTK (Mandatory Prefix)" section
- Project `CLAUDE.md` (line 9): "Hook-Aware Behavior" mentions RTK

**Cross-reference check**:

| Command | Global RTK.md | Project AGENTS.md |
|---------|---------------|------------------|
| `rtk tsc --noEmit` | line 76 | line 40 |
| `rtk npm run test` | line 102 | line 42 |
| `rtk docker compose exec` | line 93 | line 41 |
| `rtk vitest run` | line 105 | IMPLICIT (in hook) |
| Manual prefix requirement | YES (lines 14, 64-66) | YES (line 78) |
| Windows native, no hook | YES (line 13) | YES (line 9) |

**Finding**: **NO DRIFT detected**. Project AGENTS.md deliberately summarizes the critical RTK discipline into §RTK (mandatory prefix) + Self-Check, rather than re-teaching the entire 128-line reference. This is **correct abbreviation**, not duplication.

**Evidence** (line-by-line consistency):
- AGENTS.md line 78-79 ("Windows native — every Bash call whose output spans more than ~3 lines MUST start with `rtk`") mirrors global RTK.md line 13-14
- AGENTS.md line 40-42 (verification commands) match global RTK.md line 29-30, 76, 105
- AGENTS.md line 82-95 (Self-Check) maps to global RTK.md line 69-80 (MUST Prefix table)

✅ **No contradiction found.**

---

### **3. HOOK REGISTRATION CONFLICTS**

**Status**: ✅ **NO CONFLICTS DETECTED**

**Global hooks** (`C:\Users\nineonelabs003\.claude\settings.json`, lines 37-119):
- `SessionStart` / `SessionEnd` / `PostToolUse` / `UserPromptSubmit` / `PreCompact` / `PostCompact` / `Stop`
- Implemented via PowerShell scripts in `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\hooks\`

**Project hooks** (`/d/最新프로젝트/나인원랩스/퍼블/260427/.claude/settings.json`, lines 35-46):
- `PostToolUse` only (lines 36-46)
- Embedded Node.js inline hook: checks file type and runs `rtk tsc`, `rtk vitest run`, `rtk docker compose exec -T web php -l`, `npx stylelint`

**Finding**: **COMPOSITION, NOT CONFLICT**.

- Global `PostToolUse` runs drift-enqueue (async, `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\hooks\drift-enqueue.ps1`)
- Project `PostToolUse` runs file-type verification (synchronous, inline Node.js)
- Both can coexist; the project hook fires **first** (synchronous validates before drift-enqueue async enqueues)

**Evidence**:
- Project settings.json has `"permissions": { "allow": ["Bash(rtk *)", ...] }` — explicitly allows the verification commands
- Global settings.json does **not** register PostToolUse handlers on Edit/Write (only matcher is `Edit|Write`), so there is no double-check
- Project hook name is descriptive: file-type checker for `.ts/.tsx/.test.ts/.php/.scss`

✅ **No architectural conflict.**

---

### **4. SKILL & AGENT REGISTRATIONS**

**Status**: ⚠️ **AUDIT-HARNESS REFERENCED BUT NOT IMPLEMENTED**

**Expected Skills** (per AGENTS.md):

| Skill | Location | Status |
|-------|----------|--------|
| `$scene-explorer` | `/d/最新プロジェクト/나인원랩스/퍼블/260427/.claude/agents/scene-explorer.md` | ✅ **EXISTS** (lines 1-30) |

| `/new-route` | `/d/最新プロジェクト/나인원랩스/퍼블/260427/.agents/skills/new-route/SKILL.md` | ✅ **EXISTS** (lines 1-31) |
| `/audit-harness [scope]` | `NOT FOUND` | ❌ **MISSING** |

**Finding**: AGENTS.md line 57 references `/audit-harness [scope]` as a repo skill, and line 74 says "Run `/audit-harness` quarterly to enforce", but **no SKILL.md file exists** in `.agents/skills/audit-harness/`.

**Actual directory structure**:
```
/d/最新プロジェクト/나인원랩스/퍼블/260427/.agents/skills/
├── new-route/SKILL.md        ✅
├── php-explorer/SKILL.md     ✅
└── scene-explorer/SKILL.md   ✅
```

No `audit-harness/` folder.

**Evidence**:
- AGENTS.md line 52-57: Lists three skills; `/audit-harness` is #4
- AGENTS.md line 74: "Run `/audit-harness` quarterly to enforce" (imperative tone suggests it should exist)
- Project `.claude/agents/` folder (separate from `.agents/skills/`) contains only `scene-explorer.md` and `php-explorer.md` (which are agent metadata, not skills)

**Impact**: Low (skill is referenced as a quarterly audit tool, not critical path). If invoked, it will fail silently as an unknown skill.

**Recommendation**: Either:
1. Remove the `/audit-harness` reference from AGENTS.md (lines 57, 74), OR
2. Implement `.agents/skills/audit-harness/SKILL.md` with the quarterly audit logic

---

### **5. 200-LINE CAP VERIFICATION**

**Status**: ✅ **PASSED**

**AGENTS.md line 63**: `"CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md combined ≤ 200 lines."`

**Actual line counts**:
```
  26 /d/最新プロジェクト/나인원랩스/퍼블/260427/CLAUDE.md
  95 /d/最新프로젝트/나인원랩스/퍼블/260427/AGENTS.md
 ---
 121 total
```

✅ **121 lines < 200 lines. Cap met.**

---

### **6. KOREAN VS. ENGLISH LANGUAGE CONSISTENCY**

**Status**: ✅ **CONSISTENT**

**Global Rule** (CLAUDE.md line 9):
```
- DO answer the user in **Korean** (chat replies). Use English for AI-consumed artifacts: docs, hooks, plans, MEMORY topic files, AUTO marks, comments, log messages.

**Project Files**:

**Status**: ✅ **SYNCHRONIZED**

**Global RTK.md section** (lines 65-107):

- **AUTOMATION.md lines 113-131**: List 14 custom PowerShell scripts, all at `C:\Users\nineonelabs003\.claude\hooks\`.

**Evidence:**
- Default Claude Code does not ship with these hooks; they are 100% custom.
- Each script has a "reason" documented in AUTOMATION.md, but reasons are generic ("archive 60d+ plans", "detect drift") rather than incident-triggered.
- No incident log exists showing a session where "plan cleanup failed catastrophically" or "memory drift caused a mistake."

**Impact:** The setup has drifted significantly from vanilla. While functional, the stated principle (vanilla by default) is **aspirational but not actualized**.

---

#### 4. AMBIGUOUS TERMINOLOGY

##### 4.1 "D-Drive" Path Ambiguity in Project Naming
**Severity:** MEDIUM

- Project directory: `C:\Users\nineonelabs003\.claude\projects\d------------------260427\`
- Backup plan file: `/c/Users/nineonelabs003/.claude/backups/precompact-20260427-171729-unknown/plans/ai-imperative-pelican.md` contains: `"D:\.claude\hooks\session-start.ps1"`
- ARCHITECTURE.md line 94: `"Forbidden": D:\.claude\, D:/.claude-data/, or any literal D-drive reference."`

**Issue:** The project folder name `d------------------260427` **looks like it refers to the D drive**, but it's actually a C-drive path. The naming convention is opaque.

**Evidence:**
- backup .claude.json files from earlier sessions reference actual D:/ paths: `"D:/最新プロジェクト/ナインワンラボズ/パブ/260427"` (lines in backups).
- Current project structure is all on C:, but the legacy naming from the D-drive era persists.
- A human or AI reading `d------------------260427` would reasonably assume it's a D-drive path marker.

**Impact:** Confusing legacy naming. When an AI reads "d--" folder names, it might mistakenly conclude those paths are on D: drive.

---

##### 4.2 Ambiguous "Project" Scope in Permission Hierarchy
**Severity:** MEDIUM

- **ARCHITECTURE.md line 248**: `"Project .claude/settings.json deny added (Drive policy enforcement) — AGENTS.md declared D: drive only for project work... Project-level deny overrides user-level (precedence: Project > User)."`
- **settings.json** has global deny rules, but **no project-level deny files exist** (neither in global scope nor referenced in active projects).
- **project-init.md lines 126-144** show an example `settings.json` with PostToolUse hooks, but no example deny list.

**Issue:** Precedence is documented (`Project > User`), but no actual project-level deny rule exists in any `.claude/settings.json` under `projects/`. If a user tries to add one, they won't know the correct syntax or location.

**Evidence:**
- Global: `C:\Users\nineonelabs003\.claude\settings.json` has `permissions.deny` (verified, lines 6-31).
- Project: `/c/Users/nineonelabs003/.claude/projects/d------------------260427/` has session dirs but no `.claude/settings.json` (verified with `ls`).
- project-init.md mentions "settings.json" but the example shown (lines 128-143) only has hooks, no permissions block.

**Impact:** User or AI trying to implement "project-level deny override" would not know where to put it or how it works.

---

#### 5. STALE DOCUMENTATION

##### 5.1 Plan Files Contain Obsolete D-Drive References
**Severity:** LOW (backup data, not live)

- **ai-imperative-pelican.md** (in backups/precompact-*/) extensively references `D:\.claude\` paths throughout.
- **docs-restructure-bobcat.md** and **starry-skipping-crown.md** in backups also use D:\ references.

**Evidence:**
- `/c/Users/nineonelabs003/.claude/backups/precompact-20260427-171729-unknown/plans/ai-imperative-pelican.md` shows 20+ references to `D:\.claude\settings.json`, `D:\.claude\hooks\*`, etc.
- These are archived/historical plans from before the consolidation.

**Impact:** Low immediate impact (backups are read-only), but if someone re-reads these archived plans, they'll get stale guidance. The archive should either be deleted or marked with a date/status banner.

---

##### 5.2 AUTOMATION.md "Last verified" Timestamp vs. Actual Content Sync
**Severity:** LOW

- **AUTOMATION.md line 5**: `"**Last verified**: 2026-04-28T13:59:47+09:00 <!-- AUTO:TIMESTAMP -->"`
- **update-docs.ps1** is supposed to regenerate this timestamp on **every SessionStart**.
- **settings.json line 43** registers SessionStart hook, which calls `session-start.ps1`.
- **session-start.ps1 line 21** calls `update-docs.ps1`.

**Verification:** The timestamp is exactly at session start time (13:59:47), so it **is working correctly**. However, if `update-docs.ps1` is ever broken, the timestamp becomes a **lie** that makes docs appear current when they're stale.

**Impact:** Very low; the automation appears functional. This is more of a "trust but verify" note for future maintenance.

---

#### 6. ORDER OF PRECEDENCE AMBIGUITY

##### 6.1 Rule Override Hierarchy Not Fully Specified
**Severity:** MEDIUM

- **Global rules**: `C:\Users\nineonelabs003\.claude\CLAUDE.md`
- **Project memory**: `C:\Users\nineonelabs003\.claude\projects\d------------------260427\memory\*.md`
- **Settings permission precedence**: `Project > User` (ARCHITECTURE.md line 248)
- **Missing documentation**: What happens when global CLAUDE.md says "DO X" but project memory says "DON'T X"?

**Evidence:**
- CLAUDE.md line 12 says "DO verify the work matches the user's original order before declaring done" (order match verification).
- project_workflow.md implies each project should have **its own order-match checklist** (references `feedback_` topic files, which are project-specific).
- No reconciliation rule exists for when these conflict.

**Impact:** If a project MEMORY.md contradicts global CLAUDE.md, an AI agent won't know which one to follow. Example: what if global CLAUDE.md says "DON'T run `npm install`" but a project MEMORY.md says "must run `npm install <pkg>` when adding deps"? (Actual case: feedback_npm_build.md says "never run npm build/watch/install.")

---

#### 7. ENVIRONMENT-SPECIFIC STALE REFERENCES

##### 7.1 WSL References in Global Docs
**Severity:** LOW

- **CLAUDE.md line 17**: `"DON'T propose WSL workflows, install steps, or 'rtk init -g --auto-patch' hook auto-rewrite."`
- **RTK.md line 12**: `"This machine is Windows native: there is no hook auto-rewrite."`
- **RTK.md line 44**: `"DON'T set up WSL or 'rtk init -g --auto-patch'."`
- **feedback_rtk.md line 12**: `"WSL Remote: PreToolUse hook이 자동 prefix"` (in Korean, saying WSL has auto-prefix hook).

**Inconsistency:** The global rules explicitly forbid WSL setup, but **feedback_rtk.md still references WSL behavior**. This suggests it was copy-pasted from a WSL template and never updated.

**Evidence:**
- feedback_rtk.md was created in a prior session (originSessionId: f4145fdf-...) and references `"WSL Remote"` behavior.
- Current environment is 100% native Windows (verified in ARCHITECTURE.md line 16).

**Impact:** Low, since the main CLAUDE.md/RTK.md forbid WSL. But an AI reading the backup memory files (feedback_rtk.md) might get confused about whether WSL is an option.

---

### SUMMARY TABLE

| Finding | Severity | Type | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.1 D-Drive Policy Contradiction | HIGH | Contradiction | Clarify whether global AGENTS.md should exist; update ARCHITECTURE.md to distinguish "planned" from "implemented" |
| 1.2 RTK Auto-Rewrite (Documented but Not Implemented) | MEDIUM | Contradiction | Remove project-init.md example with Node.js pipe OR verify it works with actual hooks |
| 1.3 Korean Language in AI-Consumed Docs | LOW | Contradiction | Translate `project_architecture.md` to English |
| 2.1 Missing `scene-explorer` / `php-explorer` Agents | HIGH | Dangling Reference | Create agents using project-init.md format or update memory to remove references |
| 2.2 Missing Global AGENTS.md | MEDIUM | Dangling Reference | Create global AGENTS.md or remove references in CLAUDE.md/ARCHITECTURE.md |
| 2.3 @import Chain Described but Minimal Use | MEDIUM | Dangling Reference | Simplify docs; note that only RTK.md is imported currently |
| 3.1 FOMO Guard Not Documented for Hook Registry | MEDIUM | Self-Violation | Add incident/benefit justification for `permissions.defaultMode` and hook triggers |
| 3.2 Vanilla Compliance Aspirational (14 Custom Scripts) | LOW | Self-Violation | Update principle statement to reflect actual customization level |
| 4.1 D-Drive Folder Naming Ambiguity (`d--`) | MEDIUM | Ambiguity | Rename or document naming convention; clarify in ARCHITECTURE.md |
| 4.2 Project-Level Permission Hierarchy Under-Specified | MEDIUM | Ambiguity | Document actual precedence with examples; provide template in project-init.md |
| 5.1 Archived Plans with D-Drive References | LOW | Stale Docs | Delete or archive with date header (e.g., "ARCHIVED 2026-04-28: stale D-drive references") |
| 5.2 AUTOMATION.md Timestamp Automation Trust | LOW | Stale Docs | No action needed; verify on next SessionStart |
| 6.1 Rule Hierarchy for CLAUDE.md vs. Project MEMORY | MEDIUM | Precedence | Document rule precedence: Global rules > Project overrides (per-project rules in feedback_* topics) |
| 7.1 WSL References in feedback_rtk.md | LOW | Environment Stale | Update feedback_rtk.md to remove WSL-specific guidance or mark as "archived from prior environment" |

---

### RECOMMENDATIONS (PRIORITY ORDER)

**CRITICAL (Blocking clarity):**
1. **Create the referenced agents** (`scene-explorer`, `php-explorer`) using the template in project-init.md, OR remove all references from project memory files.
2. **Clarify D-drive decision:** Update ARCHITECTURE.md to state clearly whether a global AGENTS.md should exist and why it currently doesn't.
3. **Translate project_architecture.md to English** to comply with the documented language convention.

**HIGH (Confusing for future AI agents):**
4. **Document rule precedence:** Add a section to ARCHITECTURE.md explaining: Global CLAUDE.md > Project MEMORY.md `feedback_*` overrides (per-project deltas).
5. **Fix project-init.md example:** Either show actual working PostToolUse hook syntax OR note that it's a template and requires manual adjustment.

**MEDIUM (Cleanliness):**
6. **Remove or update AGENTS.md references** from CLAUDE.md line 44 and ARCHITECTURE.md line 248.
7. **Mark archived plans** with date and "D-drive era" header to prevent re-reading stale guidance.
8. **Audit FOMO Guard justifications:** Document the incident or measurable cost for `permissions.defaultMode = "bypassPermissions"`.

**LOW (Nice-to-have):**
9. Update feedback_rtk.md to remove WSL references or mark it as archived.
10. Simplify @import chain documentation or implement multi-level imports to justify the complexity.

1	# Global Claude Code Architecture
2	
3	This document describes the architecture of this machine's global Claude Code setup. Read this before changing rules, hooks, or directory layout. Companion documents:
4	
5	- `CLAUDE.md` — operating rules (DO / DON'T)
6	- `RTK.md` — token-optimized CLI proxy reference
7	- `AUTOMATION.md` — session automation hooks (architecture diagram + auto-generated tables)
8	- `templates/order-match-checklist.md` — task self-verification template
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 1. Operating Environment
13	
14	| Property | Value |
15	|---|---|
16	| OS | Windows 10 (native, no WSL) |
17	| Shell | Git Bash (primary) / PowerShell 5.1 |
18	| AI assistant | Claude Code (sole assistant — Codex / Cursor removed) |
19	| IDE host | VS Code with Claude Code extension |
20	| Drive layout | **C drive only** for all Claude artifacts (no D / E split) |
21	
22	**Rationale (single-drive on C)**: cognitive simplicity, tool universality (every Windows tool assumes `%USERPROFILE%\.claude`), and vanilla compliance with Claude Code's default. C has 88+ GB free; the entire setup is ~165 MB.
23	
24	---
25	
26	## 2. Directory Layout
27	
28	```
29	%USERPROFILE%\.claude\                     [single source of truth, plain dirs only — no junctions]
30	│
31	├── CLAUDE.md                              # operating rules (DO / DON'T)
32	├── RTK.md                                 # CLI proxy reference
33	├── AUTOMATION.md                          # session automation architecture + auto-marked tables
34	├── ARCHITECTURE.md                        # this file
35	│
36	├── settings.json                          # hook registrations + permissions + statusline
37	├── settings.local.json                    # per-host overrides (optional)
38	├── active-projects.json                   # pinned projects (cleanup.ps1 protection list)
39	├── .claude.json                           # Claude Code internal session state (autogenerated, do not edit)
40	├── .credentials.json                      # MCP auth (sensitive — never read / commit)
41	│
42	├── cleanup.ps1                            # SessionEnd cleanup + retention rotations
43	├── statusline.ps1                         # status line renderer (cwd | model | effort | sessions | warnings)
44	│
45	├── hooks/                                 # SessionStart / SessionEnd / Pre+PostCompact / PostToolUse hooks
46	├── templates/                             # project-init.md, order-match-checklist.md
47	├── plugins/                               # plugin metadata
48	├── ide/                                   # IDE settings
49	├── agents/                                # custom agent definitions (if any)
50	├── commands/                              # slash command definitions (if any)
51	│
52	├── projects/                              # per-project session state + memory
53	├── plans/                                 # active + archived plans
54	├── reports/                               # token-usage.md (append-only)
55	├── backups/                               # precompact-* snapshots + memory-YYYYWW.zip weekly
56	├── file-history/                          # UUID-keyed file version diffs
57	├── shell-snapshots/                       # shell context snapshots
58	├── sessions/                              # session state (ephemeral)
59	├── session-env/                           # SessionStart artifacts (memory-lint.txt, compact-warning.txt)
60	├── paste-cache/                           # clipboard cache (ephemeral)
61	├── downloads/                             # downloaded artifacts
62	├── telemetry/                             # telemetry queue
63	├── cache/                                 # generic cache
64	├── .docs-cache/                           # SHA256 hashes of upstream docs + prefix-version.txt
65	├── .drift-queue/                          # PostToolUse enqueue → drift-detect-worker drain
66	│
67	├── history.jsonl                          # session history log
68	└── cleanup.log                            # SessionEnd audit trail
69	
70	%USERPROFILE%\.claude-archive\             [out-of-band backups, separate from live config]
71	└── rollback-pre-consolidation.zip         # one-shot pre-D-removal snapshot
72	```
73	
74	**Anti-pattern**: do not create NTFS junctions to redirect any subdirectory to another volume. The previous D-split design was reverted because it complicated backup tooling, broke drive-letter assumptions in third-party scripts, and provided no measurable benefit at this data scale.
75	
76	---
77	
78	## 3. Path Resolution Convention
79	
80	Every script and document references the config root via:
81	
82	```powershell
83	$ClaudeRoot = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) {
84	    $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
85	} else {
86	    Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.claude'
87	}
88	```
89	
90	`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is **not set** in any registry scope — the env var fallback exists only to honor user overrides if a future need arises. The default code path always resolves to `%USERPROFILE%\.claude`.
91	
92	In documentation: use `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\` (Windows-native, expands in cmd / PowerShell / Git Bash) or `~/.claude/` for compactness.
93	
94	**Forbidden**: `D:\.claude\`, `D:/.claude-data/`, or any literal D-drive reference.
95	
96	---
97	
98	## 4. Hook Architecture
99	
100	Eight hook events are registered in `settings.json`. See `AUTOMATION.md` for the full sequence diagram and the auto-generated registration table.
101	
102	| Event | Purpose | Async |
103	|---|---|---|
104	| SessionStart | regenerate AUTO-marks, auto-pin, memory-lint, weekly memory-backup, 24h doc gate, 60d plan archive, **D-remnant detection → oneshot consolidation** | no |
105	| SessionEnd | retention rotations (13 categories), MEMORY.md link integrity, kill stale workers, drift queue drain | yes |
106	| PostToolUse (Edit\|Write\|Bash) | enqueue edited files / dep-install audits to `.drift-queue` | yes |
107	| UserPromptSubmit | inject git status + recent commits when repo is dirty (skip-when-clean keeps prompt cache warm) | no |
108	| PreCompact | hard-link snapshot of MUST-preserve set into `backups/precompact-<ts>-<sid>` | no |
109	| PostCompact | verify `@import` chains + active plan readability; write `compact-warning.txt` on issues | yes |
110	| Stop | append rtk session stats to `reports/token-usage.md` | yes |
111	| statusLine | render status line (includes `compact:warn` indicator if PostCompact flagged a loss) | (poll) |
112	
113	**Design principle**: each hook runs in <100 ms in the synchronous path. Heavier work (`check-updates-worker`) is spawned detached via `Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden`. Detached workers survive parent exit; PowerShell jobs do not.
114	
115	---
116	
117	## 5. Retention Policy
118	
119	Configured in `cleanup.ps1`. Pinned projects (via `active-projects.json`) are exempt from `projects/` rotation.
120	
121	| Directory | Retention | Notes |
122	|---|---|---|
123	| `plans/` | 2 days (file mtime) | drafts; archived plans go to `plans/archive/` after 60d |
124	| `shell-snapshots/` | 7 days | session shell context |
125	| `file-history/` | 14 days (dir mtime) | UUID-keyed |
126	| `projects/` | 30 days (dir mtime) | pinned + 14d grace exempt |
127	| `session-env/` | empty subdirs only | per-session SessionStart outputs |
128	| `backups/precompact-*` | 28 days | pre-compaction snapshots |
129	| `backups/memory-*.zip` | 56 days | weekly memory archive |
130	| `.docs-cache/` | 90 days (file mtime) | SHA hashes regenerable |
131	| `.drift-queue/` | 7 days | post-drain leftovers |
132	| `cache/` | 14 days | generic |
133	| `downloads/` | 30 days | |
134	| `paste-cache/` | 7 days | clipboard |
135	| `telemetry/` | 30 days | |
136	
137	Stale background workers >24h old are killed by command-line pattern match against `<ClaudeRoot>\hooks\`.
138	
139	---
140	
141	## 6. Compaction Policy (REWIND CONTEXT)
142	
143	When Claude Code reaches its context budget and triggers compaction:
144

# Global Claude Code Architecture

This document describes the architecture of this machine's global Claude Code setup. Read this before changing rules, hooks, or directory layout. Companion documents:

- `CLAUDE.md` — operating rules (DO / DON'T)
- `RTK.md` — token-optimized CLI proxy reference
- `AUTOMATION.md` — session automation hooks (architecture diagram + auto-generated tables)
- `templates/order-match-checklist.md` — task self-verification template

---

## 1. Operating Environment

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| OS | Windows 10 (native, no WSL) |
| Shell | Git Bash (primary) / PowerShell 5.1 |
| AI assistant | Claude Code (sole assistant — Codex / Cursor removed) |
| IDE host | VS Code with Claude Code extension |
| Drive layout | **C drive only** for all Claude artifacts (no D / E split) |

**Rationale (single-drive on C)**: cognitive simplicity, tool universality (every Windows tool assumes `%USERPROFILE%\.claude`), and vanilla compliance with Claude Code's default. C has 88+ GB free; the entire setup is ~165 MB.

---

## 2. Directory Layout

```
%USERPROFILE%\.claude\                     [single source of truth, plain dirs only — no junctions]
│
├── CLAUDE.md                              # operating rules (DO / DON'T)
├── RTK.md                                 # CLI proxy reference
├── AUTOMATION.md                          # session automation architecture + auto-marked tables
├── ARCHITECTURE.md                        # this file
│
├── settings.json                          # hook registrations + permissions + statusline
├── settings.local.json                    # per-host overrides (optional)
├── active-projects.json                   # pinned projects (cleanup.ps1 protection list)
├── .claude.json                           # Claude Code internal session state (autogenerated, do not edit)
├── .credentials.json                      # MCP auth (sensitive — never read / commit)
│
├── cleanup.ps1                            # SessionEnd cleanup + retention rotations
├── statusline.ps1                         # status line renderer (cwd | model | effort | sessions | warnings)
│
├── hooks/                                 # SessionStart / SessionEnd / Pre+PostCompact / PostToolUse hooks
├── templates/                             # project-init.md, order-match-checklist.md
├── plugins/                               # plugin metadata
├── ide/                                   # IDE settings
├── agents/                                # custom agent definitions (if any)
├── commands/                              # slash command definitions (if any)
│
├── projects/                              # per-project session state + memory
├── plans/                                 # active + archived plans
├── reports/                               # token-usage.md (append-only)
├── backups/                               # precompact-* snapshots + memory-YYYYWW.zip weekly
├── file-history/                          # UUID-keyed file version diffs
├── shell-snapshots/                       # shell context snapshots
├── sessions/                              # session state (ephemeral)
├── session-env/                           # SessionStart artifacts (memory-lint.txt, compact-warning.txt)
├── paste-cache/                           # clipboard cache (ephemeral)
├── downloads/                             # downloaded artifacts
├── telemetry/                             # telemetry queue
├── cache/                                 # generic cache
├── .docs-cache/                           # SHA256 hashes of upstream docs + prefix-version.txt
├── .drift-queue/                          # PostToolUse enqueue → drift-detect-worker drain
│
├── history.jsonl                          # session history log
└── cleanup.log                            # SessionEnd audit trail

%USERPROFILE%\.claude-archive\             [out-of-band backups, separate from live config]
└── rollback-pre-consolidation.zip         # one-shot pre-D-removal snapshot
```

**Anti-pattern**: do not create NTFS junctions to redirect any subdirectory to another volume. The previous D-split design was reverted because it complicated backup tooling, broke drive-letter assumptions in third-party scripts, and provided no measurable benefit at this data scale.

---

## 3. Path Resolution Convention

Every script and document references the config root via:

```powershell
$ClaudeRoot = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) {
    $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
} else {
    Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.claude'
}
```

`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is **not set** in any registry scope — the env var fallback exists only to honor user overrides if a future need arises. The default code path always resolves to `%USERPROFILE%\.claude`.

In documentation: use `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\` (Windows-native, expands in cmd / PowerShell / Git Bash) or `~/.claude/` for compactness.

**Forbidden**: `D:\.claude\`, `D:/.claude-data/`, or any literal D-drive reference.

---

## 4. Hook Architecture

Eight hook events are registered in `settings.json`. See `AUTOMATION.md` for the full sequence diagram and the auto-generated registration table.

| Event | Purpose | Async |
|---|---|---|
| SessionStart | regenerate AUTO-marks, auto-pin, memory-lint, weekly memory-backup, 24h doc gate, 60d plan archive, **D-remnant detection → oneshot consolidation** | no |
| SessionEnd | retention rotations (13 categories), MEMORY.md link integrity, kill stale workers, drift queue drain | yes |
| PostToolUse (Edit\|Write\|Bash) | enqueue edited files / dep-install audits to `.drift-queue` | yes |
| UserPromptSubmit | inject git status + recent commits when repo is dirty (skip-when-clean keeps prompt cache warm) | no |
| PreCompact | hard-link snapshot of MUST-preserve set into `backups/precompact-<ts>-<sid>` | no |
| PostCompact | verify `@import` chains + active plan readability; write `compact-warning.txt` on issues | yes |
| Stop | append rtk session stats to `reports/token-usage.md` | yes |
| statusLine | render status line (includes `compact:warn` indicator if PostCompact flagged a loss) | (poll) |

**Design principle**: each hook runs in <100 ms in the synchronous path. Heavier work (`check-updates-worker`) is spawned detached via `Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden`. Detached workers survive parent exit; PowerShell jobs do not.

---

Configured in `cleanup.ps1`. Pinned projects (via `active-projects.json`) are exempt from `projects/` rotation.

| Directory | Retention | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `plans/` | 2 days (file mtime) | drafts; archived plans go to `plans/archive/` after 60d |
| `shell-snapshots/` | 7 days | session shell context |
| `file-history/` | 14 days (dir mtime) | UUID-keyed |
| `projects/` | 30 days (dir mtime) | pinned + 14d grace exempt |
| `session-env/` | empty subdirs only | per-session SessionStart outputs |
| `backups/precompact-*` | 28 days | pre-compaction snapshots |
| `backups/memory-*.zip` | 56 days | weekly memory archive |
| `.docs-cache/` | 90 days (file mtime) | SHA hashes regenerable |
| `.drift-queue/` | 7 days | post-drain leftovers |
| `cache/` | 14 days | generic |
| `downloads/` | 30 days | |
| `paste-cache/` | 7 days | clipboard |
| `telemetry/` | 30 days | |

Stale background workers >24h old are killed by command-line pattern match against `<ClaudeRoot>\hooks\`.

---

## 6. Compaction Policy (REWIND CONTEXT)

When Claude Code reaches its context budget and triggers compaction:

**MUST preserve** (load-bearing): active plan, all rule files (`CLAUDE.md` / `RTK.md` / `AUTOMATION.md` / `ARCHITECTURE.md`), `settings.json`, per-project active `MEMORY.md`, memory topic files modified within last 30 days.

- **Coverage**: noisy multi-line outputs (`git`, `docker`, `tsc`, test runners, `find`, log files, `gh pr`, package managers).
- **Skip**: single-line outputs (`echo`, `pwd`).

Detailed savings table: see `RTK.md`.

---

## 8. Order Match Verification

Every non-trivial task ends with a self-verification step before the AI declares completion. Procedure (full template at `templates/order-match-checklist.md`):

2. List acceptance criteria (observable state).
3. Map each criterion to evidence (`file:line`, command output, test result).
4. Detect scope creep — anything done outside the order? Justify or revert.
5. Honor constraints — language (Korean chat / English AI artifacts), paths (no `D:\.claude`), tools, banned actions.

If any criterion lacks evidence: do **not** declare done. Either complete the gap or report it explicitly.

This rule is the system's primary safeguard against the "AI says done but didn't actually finish" failure mode.

---

## 9. Vanilla Compliance + FOMO Guard

---

## 10. AI Tool Exclusivity

6. **Permission glob**: `rtk grep "Read(.credentials" C:\Users\nineonelabs003\.claude\settings.json` shows the `**/` recursive form.

Open one fresh Claude Code session after the edits and watch the SessionStart hook output for any `compact-warning.txt` or `memory-lint.txt` complaints — those would surface broken links or unreadable files introduced by the edits.

- `/audit-harness` SKILL.md creation (referenced in project AGENTS.md L57/L74 but not implemented). Deferred.

- **Stop**: append rtk session stats to `reports\token-usage.md`.
- **statusLine**: cwd-leaf | model | effort | session count | compact warning.
- **env**: `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1` only (vanilla baseline). `prefix-version.txt` is bumped on rule changes to invalidate stale cache.

## RTK on This Machine

Windows native — no auto-rewrite. Type `rtk <command>` explicitly when noisy output is expected. RTK passes unknown commands through unchanged, so prefixing is always safe.

## Permission-Mode Caveat

`permissions.defaultMode = "bypassPermissions"` + `skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt = true` are active. **Safe only inside Docker / isolated environments.** When working directly on the host, the safety net relies on `permissions.deny` (`rm -rf`, force push, hard reset, `.credentials`); keep `settings.json` in sync when adding new deny entries.

---
name: NINEONELABS Project Architecture
description: Core architecture decisions — custom MVC, Three.js scene structure, Theatre.js binding locations, bfcache pattern, SEO files
type: project
originSessionId: 9bdf7fa7-352d-44ea-97bc-694667eeaecf
---
Custom PHP 7.4 MVC + Three.js + Theatre.js web agency site renewal project.

**Key architecture decisions:**
- Routing: closure-based (`routes/web.php` + `render()`) — NOT controller-class MVC
- Three.js scenes: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/scene/`
- Theatre.js bindings: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/theatre/`
- Shared code: outside page folders (`resource/ts/runtime/`, `resource/ts/manager/`, etc.)
- TypeScript types: dedicated `resource/ts/types/*.types.ts` files — no inline types, no `any`
- Build: Vite (bundle) + sass CLI (CSS) — never run `npm run build` (dev server auto-rebuilds on save)
- DB tables: `nb_` prefix (e.g. `nb_siteinfo`, `nb_admin`)

**Notable shared utilities (resource/ts/):**

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `app/ResizeSetup.ts` | resize debounce + visualViewport sync |
| `runtime/SubpageStarfieldRuntime.ts` | shared 3D starfield parallax for contact / careers / inside |
| `ui/WorkCard.ts` | canvas-based texture rendering helper for WorkCard |
| `utils/Device.ts` | device / viewport detection (includes iOS visualViewport) |
| `utils/PerformanceProfile.ts` | automatic performance tier selection (low / mid / high) |

**bfcache support pattern (settled 2026-04-24):**
- Restart / tear down RAF chains via `pageshow` and `pagehide` events
- Applied across `app.ts`, `AnimationLoop.ts`, `LenisRuntime.ts`, `SubpageStarfieldRuntime.ts`
- Do not use `beforeunload` (it disables bfcache entry)

**Author / editor mode pattern:**
- `data-*-mode="author"` attribute → isolated UI via `_utils.scss` selectors
- During Theatre.js Studio editing, header / panel / intro elements get `pointer-events: none` + transparency

**SEO infrastructure:**
- `robots.txt`: blocks admin / api paths, includes sitemap reference
- `views/pages/sitemap.php`: dynamic XML sitemap for works / news / insight / award

**Why:** Designed to eliminate Barba.js / SPA contracts and enforce clear ownership separation between AppManager, PageRuntime, and PageTheatreBinder.

**How to apply:** Always follow this structure when adding new pages or features. Use the `/new-route` skill.

- Routing: closure-based (`routes/web.php` + `render()`) — NOT controller-class MVC
- Three.js scenes: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/scene/`
- Theatre.js bindings: `resource/ts/pages/<page>/theatre/`
- Shared code: outside page folders (`resource/ts/runtime/`, `resource/ts/manager/`, etc.)
- TypeScript types: dedicated `resource/ts/types/*.types.ts` files — no inline types, no `any`
- Build: Vite (bundle) + sass CLI (CSS) — never run `npm run build` (dev server auto-rebuilds on save)
- DB tables: `nb_` prefix (e.g. `nb_siteinfo`, `nb_admin`)

**Notable shared utilities (resource/ts/):**

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `app/ResizeSetup.ts` | resize debounce + visualViewport sync |
| `runtime/SubpageStarfieldRuntime.ts` | shared 3D starfield parallax for contact / careers / inside |
| `ui/WorkCard.ts` | canvas-based texture rendering helper for WorkCard |
| `utils/Device.ts` | device / viewport detection (includes iOS visualViewport) |
| `utils/PerformanceProfile.ts` | automatic performance tier selection (low / mid / high) |

**bfcache support pattern (settled 2026-04-24):**
- Restart / tear down RAF chains via `pageshow` and `pagehide` events
- Applied across `app.ts`, `AnimationLoop.ts`, `LenisRuntime.ts`, `SubpageStarfieldRuntime.ts`
- Do not use `beforeunload` (it disables bfcache entry)

**Author / editor mode pattern:**
- `data-*-mode="author"` attribute → isolated UI via `_utils.scss` selectors
- During Theatre.js Studio editing, header / panel / intro elements get `pointer-events: none` + transparency

**SEO infrastructure:**
- `robots.txt`: blocks admin / api paths, includes sitemap reference
- `views/pages/sitemap.php`: dynamic XML sitemap for works / news / insight / award

**Why:** Designed to eliminate Barba.js / SPA contracts and enforce clear ownership separation between AppManager, PageRuntime, and PageTheatreBinder.

**How to apply:** Always follow this structure when adding new pages or features. Use the `/new-route` skill.

# Claude Code Harness Setup Checklist

One-time setup health check for the Claude Code harness in this project. Code-writing guidelines live in `.claude/BEST_PRACTICES.md`.

---

## 1. CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md

- [x] `CLAUDE.md` under 30 lines (current: ~26)?
- [x] `CLAUDE.md` + `AGENTS.md` combined ≤ 200 lines? (Anthropic loads both every session — hard cap.)
- [x] Does not contain anything Claude can infer from reading the code (file structure, naming conventions, etc.)?
- [x] File-type rules are separated into `.claude/rules/` with `paths:` frontmatter (lazy load)?
- [x] Each prohibition is verifiable by lint / tsc / test / grep?
- [x] Verification commands included (tsc, lint, test, etc.)?

## 2. Rules (`.claude/rules/`)

- [x] Split by file extension? (`php.md`, `frontend.md`, `scss.md`)
- [x] Each rules file has a `paths:` frontmatter header?
- [x] Rules contain only things that cannot be inferred from the code?

## 3. Hooks (`.claude/settings.json`)

- [x] Auto-runs tsc after editing a `.ts` file?
- [x] Hook verified to actually fire by editing a `.ts` file?
- [x] Frequently used safe commands registered in `allowedTools`?

## 4. Skills (`.claude/skills/`)

- [x] Repeatable workflows packaged as skills?
- [x] `/new-route` defined (multi-step page creation procedure)?

## Permission setup — `allowDangerouslySkipPermissions`

To prevent Claude Code from asking for permission on every action, enable via VS Code:

1. Open **File → Preferences → Settings** (or `Ctrl+,`)
2. Search for `claudeCode.allowDangerouslySkipPermissions`
3. Check the box — this adds "Bypass permissions" to the mode cycle

> **Warning:** This flag auto-approves all tool use: file writes, Bash execution, etc.
> Use only in trusted projects. Default permission mode is recommended for unfamiliar codebases.

## Why npm build commands are forbidden

`npm run build`, `npm run watch`, and `npm install` are **forbidden during normal development**.

- **Reason:** Vite dev server at `http://localhost:8888` auto-rebuilds the bundle on every file save
- Running these wastes context and time with no benefit
- **Exception:** `npm install <package>` — only when explicitly adding a new dependency
- Single source of truth: `.claude/rules/frontend.md` (auto-loads on `.ts`/`.tsx` edits via `paths:` frontmatter). AGENTS.md points here in one line — do not restate.

## How the tsc PostToolUse hook works

When a `.ts` file is modified via the Edit or Write tool, the PostToolUse hook fires automatically:

```bash
# Command executed by the hook
rtk tsc --noEmit
```

- Hook config: `.claude/settings.json` → `PostToolUse` → matcher: `Edit|Write`
- If tsc errors are found, the hook returns `exit(1)`, immediately notifying Claude
- **How to verify:** Edit any `.ts` file with the Edit tool → check hook output for tsc results

## 8. Permission strategy

Three layers, pick the lightest one that still keeps you in the loop.

| Mode | When | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `allowDangerouslySkipPermissions` | Trusted local repo work (current default) | VS Code setting — already enabled, see §"Permission setup" above |
| `/permissions` allowlist | Untrusted code, external PR review, shared boxes | Run `/permissions` and approve specific tools (`rtk git *`, `rtk tsc`, etc.) instead of blanket bypass |
| Default prompt-per-action | First time on a strange branch, when investigating supply-chain risk | No flag — Claude asks before each Bash/MCP call |

Rules of thumb:

- **Never** add a tool to the global allowlist that can write outside the repo (e.g., `rm -rf /`, `aws *`). Keep blast radius local.
- New MCP server: `claude mcp add <name>` then verify entry in `.claude/settings.json`. Document the why in this file before committing.
- `gh` CLI is preferred over raw GitHub API — it handles auth, avoids rate limits, and keeps PR/issue work out of the browser. Install with `winget install --id GitHub.cli` if missing.
- Forbidden flags regardless of mode: `--no-verify`, `--no-gpg-sign`, `git push --force` to `main`. Hooks and signatures are not optional.
